steps.text: Combine milk, eggs, sugar, vanilla extract, and nutmeg together in a blender and process until well combined; transfer to a large pitcher.

raw_recipe.headline: Easiest Eggnog
raw_recipe.description: This easiest eggnog recipe is made with milk, eggs, sugar, vanilla, and nutmeg for a creamy, festive drink — delicious on its own or spiked with brandy.
raw_recipe.name: Easiest Eggnog

recipeInstructions.text: Combine milk, eggs, sugar, vanilla extract, and nutmeg together in a blender and process until well combined; transfer to a large pitcher.

review.reviewBody:
I have been making this eggnog ever since finding it in a Home Economics Cookbook "So- you are ready to cook" by Mary Ann Duffie. 
To the reviewer who gave a low rating because it was not "thick", this is NOT meant to be "thick", if you like it that thick, try using sweetened condensed milk. 
The only changes I made (to make 1 serving) I used 1 egg, 1 Tbsp sugar, 1 Cup of milk, 1/4 tsp vanilla, a few grains of salt, and added whipped cream and nutmeg for that special touch. I have never had any issues finding egg chunks, as another reviewer mentioned. I find it helps to thoroughly whip the eggs first
I am so glad I found this recipe, I was about to submit the one from my old cookbook. It is definately the easiest egg nog out there, and I've never had any illness from consuming the raw eggs. Thanks for posting!

I thought it tasted more like melted vanilla ice cream, so after a taste test, I added one more egg, nutmeg, a dash of sea salt, and cinnamon (like other reviewers did) and that really made it taste like eggnog. when I make it again, I'll do 1 egg to 1 c milk - gives it that traditional creamy golden color too. I put all ingredients in my Ninja and hit the blend button - easy peasy, perfect (does need to settle a bit if you don't want a lot of foam).

My husband waits for fall to roll around every year to buy eggnog. I made this for him today and he said he will never go back to store bought again. 
I didn't have whole milk so I used 2 cups of 2% milk, and 1/3 cup of heavy whipping cream. Added a smidge more nutmeg.
Blended the eggs first in his ninja bullet and then added other ingredients, blended on Blend IQ for 2 cycles. 
Super amazing, and fresh tasting. 
Not worried about the raw eggs, but if you are you can temper them with heated milk and cook them over steam. Enjoy.

I made two batches. I made the first batch exactly as the recipe states except I had to substitute alternative milk for regular cow's milk and we didn't have any nutmeg. The alternative milk flavor came through way too strong so for my second batch I used some of the ideas in the comments. The second time I put two whole eggs in a bowl, whipped those lightly, added one cup of creamy oatmilk and one cup of heavy whipping cream, 3 tablespoons of sugar, 1 teaspoon baking vanilla, a dash of salt, and a generous sprinkling of cinnamon. I blended it with a stick blender for one minute. It turned out great.

This is how I make eggnog and the family loves it. Only change, I put it all in a blender with about 2 cups of ice and blend well. It makes if frothy and cold. If you want to kick it up a notch or two, you can drizzel in brandy and rum (dark) as it is blending. That makes it get even more frothy and tasty. Pour into mugs or glasses and top with some more grated nutmeg.

I basically have made this, as my mother and hers before her. Dash of salt 1C whole milk per egg and a kitchen teaspoon of white sugar and a quick splash of Vanilla. Decide on quantity needed, whip (I use a hand cranked egg beater) egg(s) with the salt and Vanilla to a frothy foam top. Add sugar and whip again. Add the milk and once again whip. When complete, pour into glasses or cups and add nutmeg on top as desired.

Haven't drank yet-but what I did was cook the milk with light cream, and whipped the eggs, (separated the egg white from the yoke, then whipped both to a froth), then added the milk and cream along with sugar, and cooked to well blended. I can give a better rating when I drink it after it cools.

Delish! For all of those who had a bad experience, here's a tip to help!
1. Beat the eggs first, and completely smooth with an electric beater with a whisk attachment or the regular beaters, or make sure you beat it completely smooth by hand with a whisk.
2. Add in the sugar to the eggs and mix it well for about a minute.
3. Add everything else and it's super smooth with no egg chunks!(: 

Thank you for this recipe! Simple and yummy!

I prefer eggnog on the thick side so I utilized some of the recommendations from other reviewers: added 1/4 c. of vanilla instant pudding, and a couple of ice cubes. Although these additions helped to thicken it a bit, It was still on the thinner side, With a "few" dashes of nutmeg and cinnamon to taste. I got it to the point that i really liked the flavor. Next, I will put it in the freezer and re-blend to see how thick that makes it.

I saw the comments about the consistency of this and with these modifications, I was very pleased with the outcome. I added 1/2 package of vanilla pudding, substituted the 2.3 cups of milk with 1 cup of milk, 1 cup of half and half and 1/3 cup of heavy cream. I also used three eggs instead of two. A quick and delicious recipe, plus some rum....
We didn't have enough milk, so we used 2 parts milk , one part heavy cream, one part buttermilk. it was DELICIOUS!
Needed this recipe simple for me.

I ended up using 3 cups of whole milk and 4 eggs and doubled the vanilla. I also put a few dashes of cinnamon and nutmeg. With a rich store bought egg nog, I have to add milk to it to dilute some so this came out just how I like it.
I used sweeter instead of sugar and it is great. Not the same but still very good.
I've been making this for years!!!
I LOVE eggnog!!! But, I didn't care for this recipe. I even separated the eggs and beat the whites before folding everything in so it was thicker. I just don't think it tastes anything like eggnog.
Tasted great
So very easy to make. I made mine with lactaid milk. Added some cinnamon and a little nutmeg. Thank you so much. After a taste test, I found it delicious. Now I can make it at home and save money to.
Grammy loved making this at Christmas
ty..and fun too!
